title: Frugal LLM widgets — seed ideas and rough PRD
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad exploring a small, composable feature set we can ship quickly for customers who want low-cost, embeddable LLM-powered UI components (chat snippets, summarizers, intent extractors) that have explicit token budgets and graceful quality fallbacks. Not a formal PRD — rough scope, user stories, acceptance criteria, and experiments to try.

Problem statement:
- Many customers want to add a single LLM-driven card or widget to a product page (FAQ answer, policy summarizer, short assistant) but are unwilling to pay full hosted API per-token costs for full fidelity models.
- Current ways to reduce cost (custom prompts, smaller models) are ad hoc and leak into UX. Need first-class primitives that make cost/quality tradeoffs visible and controlled.

High-level objective:
- Build a small "Frugal Widget" surface: a lightweight SDK + server config that lets teams create mini LLM experiences with explicit cost tiers, token budgets, and built-in fallback behavior. Target 2-week prototype, 8-week beta.

Success metrics (initial):
- Time to integrate widget into customer sandbox < 2 hours
- Average token spend per widget interaction < 35 tokens baseline
- Latency p50 < 350ms for cheap tier, < 100ms for premium tier
- 10 pilot customers opt into beta within 6 weeks

Persona sketches:
- Product-manager at SMB SaaS: wants a short FAQ answer card that doesn't blast their bill.
- Growth/Marketing: wants a short creative blurb generator for landing pages with manual quota.
- Platform engineer: wants predictable per-user spend and safe fallbacks to avoid spikes.

Core ideas / primitives:
1) Token budget envelope: per-widget config for max_prompt_tokens and max_response_tokens + a global monthly micro-credit bucket. Widgets automatically decline or degrade output if budget would be exceeded.

2) Quality tiers: "cheap" (quantized small open model), "balanced" (mid-size model with short context), "quality" (full model). SDK exposes tier selection but server-side routing enforces quotas and fallback rules.

3) Response slicing / micro-answer: produce ultra-short responses first (1–3 sentences) followed by optional expansions (user can click to expand; expansions charge additional tokens). Good for landing pages and previews.

4) Deterministic fallbacks: if cheap tier fails heuristics (low confidence or hallucination score), fall back to a canned template or rerank from cache rather than immediately hitting premium.

5) Hint tokens and prefetching: allow page to prefetch a 16-token hint at page load when safe, warming cache and reducing cold-start tokens for quick interactions.

6) Compact telemetry + cost labels: widget UI shows (small) cost indicator; server emits per-widget token delta and reason codes (prefetch, expand, fallback).

MVP surface (what to build first):
- JS SDK component (React-friendly) with props: model_tier, token_budget, expandable(boolean), max_preview_tokens.
- Server-side lightweight routing and quota check API + simple policy DSL: if budget_exhausted -> fallback: canned; if hallucination_risk > x -> rerank cache; else process.
- A/B experiment hook to track user engagement and incremental token spend for expansion flows.

User stories (rough):
- PM: "As a PM, I want to drop a FAQ widget on a pricing page that returns a 2-sentence answer and a link to full docs. I want to cap monthly spend for that widget to $X." Acceptance: widget returns <= 3 sentence preview, never exceeds token_budget for preview, UI shows cost estimate.
- Growth: "As a marketer, I want a landing-blurb generator that offers 3 variations, cheapest option by default, and an expand button that generates long-form only if clicked." Acceptance: default shows 3 short variations, expand triggers a second request charged separately.
- Eng: "As an engineer, I want SDK integration to fail-safe to canned copy when the model times out or budget is exceeded." Acceptance: timeouts and budget violations return canned copy without app crash.

Edge cases / constraints:
- Abuse: public pages could be scraped/abused to exhaust micro-credits — need site-level rate limits and captcha gating for free tiers.
- Consistency: expansions should be deterministically tied to preview content where possible (use same seed/temperature mapping) to avoid mismatch surprises.
- Data residency: widget config must respect private deployment constraints for enterprise customers.

Telemetry & rollout signals to collect:
- Preview accept rate (users who expand) by widget type and page
- Tokens used per preview vs expansion
- Fallback rate to canned copy or premium model
- Latency percentiles by tier
- Cost per engaged user (tokens per converted expand or click)

Experiment matrix (early):
- Variation A: preview 25 tokens + expand (pay) vs Variation B: preview 45 tokens (no expand) — measure conversion and cost efficiency.
- Variation: cheap-tier vs balanced-tier for preview quality; measure fallback rate and user satisfaction.

Acceptance criteria for beta release:
- SDK + example integration in docs repo (one React example)
- Server policy DSL supports at least: budget check, fallback-to-canned, rerank-from-cache, tier-routing
- Observability: token events emitted, fallback events tagged, experiment hooks wired to analytics
- Security: site-rate-limits + opt-in captcha gating for anonymous traffic

Implementation notes / quick architecture:
- Reuse existing routing and fallback primitives in InferRouter (can be small new policy + slot).
- Add a lightweight widget-service that stores per-widget budget counters (Redis) and emits token events.
- Previews should prefer KV-cache hits to avoid token cost when possible (generate answer, store compressed summary as preview).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Pricing for micro-credits: per-1k micro-credit pricing? flat monthly allotment? need finance input. (ask Ravi)
- UX microcopy: how explicit should cost be? small badge vs modal explaining cost. (ask Talia)
- Can we create a cheap deterministic summarizer model that reliably fits 8–16 tokens for previews? (ask Applied ML)
- Abuse detection: what heuristics are necessary to stop scraping while not blocking legitimate traffic?

Next steps (my plan):
- Quick spike: build prototype JS widget that calls a stubbed endpoint; demo in next product sync (2 weeks)
- Align with infra on quota counters and Redis schema (sync with Noah)
- Draft small confluence page: frugal-widgets-ideation (copy from this pad + sketches)

Notes-to-self: keep this small and opinionated. The goal is one composable surface with strong defaults for cost so customers don't have to reason about tokens. Ship simple fallbacks first.

End of scratchpad.
